newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian competitiveness to improve, report says.
newsitem.headline: Canadian competitiveness to improve, report says.

text.p: Improvements to Canada's fiscal health will give Canadian companies a new competitive advantage in international business, Canada's largest bank said in a report on Wednesday.
A Royal Bank of Canada survey studying the debt-to-GDP ratios of G-7 nations concluded that Canada is poised to enter a period of falling government debt and debt service charges.
"A lower debt means some combination of lower taxes and higher government spending in comparison to our neighbors to the south," said John McCallum, the bank's chief economist.
"This could certainly be an important plus in our struggle to locate business and jobs in Canada in the context of NAFTA and subsequent trade agreements," McCallum added.
Younger Canadians also are expected to benefit from lower debt-to-GDP ratio because of a lesser need to increase taxes on the working population of the future, the report said.
"The lower debt-to-GDP ratio will result in a fiscal dividend needed by the younger generation to support an aging population," McCallum said.
Canada will have the lowest debt ration of all G-7 countries, if the Canadian government's revenue and program spending grows in line with the economy, the report said.
